meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where).
+ accusative (where to).

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone.
Neuter всё.
Plural все.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.
She's always like that.
There's always a way out.
She's offended. She's always like that.

вставать.gloss: to get up, to stand up

meanings.note: Out of bed or from the floor.

examples.trans: Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
I get up at seven in the morning.
Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet.

examples.trans: See you!
I have a meeting.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit.

examples.trans: You have visitors!
We're going visiting.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: + genitive.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Ещё больше = even more.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Morning meal.

examples.trans: You are having a romantic breakfast here.

examples.text: Что у нас сегодня на завтрак?
examples.trans: What do we have for breakfast today?

examples.text: Свежие ягоды, кофе! У вас тут романтический завтрак.
examples.trans: Fresh berries, coffee! You are having a romantic breakfast here.

meanings.note: Location.

examples.trans: I'm here.
We live here.
But we're in business here.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day.

examples.trans: Every day.
Every person.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: to provide food for someone or something

examples.trans: The cook feeds the guests a delicious lunch.

examples.text: Быстро беги на кухню и корми людей!
examples.trans: Quickly run to the kitchen and feed people!

examples.text: Ты кормишь рыбу лучше наших гостей.
examples.trans: You feed the fish better than our guests.
This is my bed.
Foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: predicative: мне лень = I can't be bothered

examples.trans: They're too lazy to come down to the restaurant!
I can't be bothered to cook.

related.gloss: to be too lazy (to do sth)

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

находиться.gloss: to be located, to be found

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated
meanings.note: Imperfective reflexive verb.

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?
The town is situated on a river.
Where is the operating room located here?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.
A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.
Our hotel has to impress the guests.

examples.text: В нашем отеле действует новая услуга.
examples.trans: Our hotel has a new service.

examples.text: Кто бы мог подумать, что буду управлять отелем?
examples.trans: Who'd have thought I'd be running a hotel?

meanings.note: отличаться от + gen.; чем отличается...? = what's the difference...?

meanings.en: to be distinguished by, stand out

examples.trans: What's different about a hotel restaurant?

examples.text: Этот соус сильно отличается от классического.
examples.trans: This sauce is very different from the classic one.

meanings.note: Takes the instrumental.

examples.trans: I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Irregular plural повара.

examples.trans: There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: person visiting a person, place, or institution

examples.trans: A visitor was sitting in the reception room.

examples.text: Это журнал посетителей мэрии из полицейских вещдоков.
examples.trans: This is the mayor's visitor log from police evidence.

examples.text: Зато в ресторане станет больше посетителей.
examples.trans: On the other hand, there will be more patrons in the restaurant.
They're also guests of the hotel.
The guests are complaining about the loud noise.

при.gloss: in the presence of, by, at

meanings.en: in the presence of, at, attached to
meanings.note: + prepositional; ни при чём = has nothing to do with it / not to blame

examples.trans: The child isn't to blame.
And what does Lyolya have to do with it?

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.en: to have to, be forced to

examples.text: Всё приходится делать самой на этой кухне.
examples.trans: I have to do everything myself in this kitchen.
You have to pay for any deception.
She has to work a lot.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.trans: I work as mayor.
Where do you work?

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Рано умер = died young / too early.

examples.text: Муж тоже там работал. И рано умер.
examples.trans: My husband worked there too. And he died young.
Tomorrow I need to get up early.

examples.text: Что, по домам? Мне завтра рано вставать.
examples.trans: What, time to go home? I have to get up early tomorrow.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

спуститься.gloss: to go down, to come down

meanings.en: to go down, to come down (downstairs)

examples.trans: They're too lazy to come down to the restaurant!

examples.text: Подожди меня внизу, я сейчас спущусь.
examples.trans: Wait for me downstairs, I'll be right down.

meanings.note: As opposed to before.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: Утром = in the morning.

examples.trans: Good morning!
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.trans: He's older than me.
Better late than never.

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
examples.trans: Why not? A sales assistant earns more than a lecturer.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!
